claim: Murine studies have linked TGF-β signaling to emphysema.
source: Murine studies have linked TGF-β signaling to emphysema, and human genome-wide association studies (GWAS) studies of lung function and COPD have identified associated regions near genes in the TGF-β superfamily.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on murine models.

claim: Human genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of lung function and COPD have identified associated regions near genes in the TGF-β superfamily.
source: Murine studies have linked TGF-β signaling to emphysema, and human genome-wide association studies (GWAS) studies of lung function and COPD have identified associated regions near genes in the TGF-β superfamily.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior GWAS studies.

claim: The functional regulatory mechanisms at GWAS loci near TGF-β superfamily genes have not been identified.
source: However, the functional regulatory mechanisms at these loci have not been identified.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field prior to this study.

claim: The study performed the largest GWAS of emphysema patterns to date.
source: We performed the largest GWAS of emphysema patterns to date, identifying 10 GWAS loci including an association peak spanning a 200 kb region downstream from TGFB2.
evidence: This is a claim about the study design and scale.

claim: The GWAS identified 10 loci associated with emphysema patterns.
source: We performed the largest GWAS of emphysema patterns to date, identifying 10 GWAS loci including an association peak spanning a 200 kb region downstream from TGFB2.
evidence: This is supported by the GWAS data presented in the manuscript.

claim: One GWAS association peak spans a 200 kb region downstream from TGFB2.
source: We performed the largest GWAS of emphysema patterns to date, identifying 10 GWAS loci including an association peak spanning a 200 kb region downstream from TGFB2.
evidence: This is supported by the GWAS data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Integrative analysis of publicly available eQTL, DNaseI, and chromatin conformation data identified rs1690789 as a putative functional variant that may regulate TGFB2 expression in human fibroblasts.
source: Integrative analysis of publicly available eQTL, DNaseI, and chromatin conformation data identified a putative functional variant, rs1690789, that may regulate TGFB2 expression in human fibroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by integrative analysis of multiple data sources.

claim: The region containing rs1690789 contacts the TGFB2 promoter in fibroblasts.
source: Using chromatin conformation capture, we confirmed that the region containing rs1690789 contacts the TGFB2 promoter in fibroblasts, and CRISPR/Cas-9 targeted deletion of a ~ 100 bp region containing rs1690789 resulted in decreased TGFB2 expression in primary human lung fibroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by chromatin conformation capture experiments.

claim: CRISPR/Cas-9 targeted deletion of a ~100 bp region containing rs1690789 resulted in decreased TGFB2 expression in primary human lung fibroblasts.
source: Using chromatin conformation capture, we confirmed that the region containing rs1690789 contacts the TGFB2 promoter in fibroblasts, and CRISPR/Cas-9 targeted deletion of a ~ 100 bp region containing rs1690789 resulted in decreased TGFB2 expression in primary human lung fibroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by CRISPR/Cas-9 deletion experiments.

claim: The data provide novel mechanistic evidence linking genetic variation affecting the TGF-β pathway to emphysema in humans.
source: These data provide novel mechanistic evidence linking genetic variation affecting the TGF-β pathway to emphysema in humans.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Emphysema is pathologic destruction of lung parenchyma resulting in airspace enlargement.
source: Emphysema, that is pathologic destruction of lung parenchyma resulting in airspace enlargement, is one of the major manifestations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
evidence: This is a definition based on established medical knowledge.

claim: Emphysema is one of the major manifestations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
source: Emphysema, that is pathologic destruction of lung parenchyma resulting in airspace enlargement, is one of the major manifestations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
evidence: This is based on established medical knowledge.

claim: Emphysema occurs in distinct pathologic patterns.
source: Emphysema occurs in distinct pathologic patterns, but these patterns are not captured by traditional quantitative measures of emphysema from lung computed tomography (CT).
evidence: This is based on established medical knowledge.

claim: Distinct emphysema patterns are not captured by traditional quantitative measures of emphysema from lung computed tomography (CT).
source: Emphysema occurs in distinct pathologic patterns, but these patterns are not captured by traditional quantitative measures of emphysema from lung computed tomography (CT).
evidence: This is based on prior research and knowledge.

claim: Novel image extraction techniques were developed to quantify distinct patterns of emphysema based on the analysis of local lung density histograms.
source: In order to have more detailed radiographic measures of emphysema, we developed novel image extraction techniques to quantify the distinct patterns of emphysema based on the analysis of local lung density histograms (Mendoza, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Local histogram emphysema (LHE) measures are more predictive of clinical outcomes than standard CT emphysema quantifications.
source: These local histogram emphysema (LHE) measures are more predictive of clinical outcomes than standard CT emphysema quantifications (Castaldi et al., 2013), and in a previous genome-wide association study (GWAS) we identified genome-wide significant associations with these distinct LHE patterns (Castaldi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: A previous GWAS identified genome-wide significant associations with distinct LHE patterns.
source: These local histogram emphysema (LHE) measures are more predictive of clinical outcomes than standard CT emphysema quantifications (Castaldi et al., 2013), and in a previous genome-wide association study (GWAS) we identified genome-wide significant associations with these distinct LHE patterns (Castaldi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The mechanisms by which GWAS loci affect emphysema patterns are unknown.
source: However, the mechanisms by which these GWAS loci affect emphysema patterns are unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The majority of GWAS-identified loci for genetically complex diseases are located in non-coding DNA.
source: The majority of GWAS-identified loci for genetically complex diseases are located in non-coding DNA and influence gene regulatory elements (Maurano et al., 2012; Nicolae et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: GWAS-identified loci for genetically complex diseases influence gene regulatory elements.
source: The majority of GWAS-identified loci for genetically complex diseases are located in non-coding DNA and influence gene regulatory elements (Maurano et al., 2012; Nicolae et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: For functional characterization of emphysema GWAS loci, it is necessary to localize causal variants in regulatory elements and identify the gene(s) regulated by that element.
source: Thus, for the functional characterization of emphysema GWAS loci, it is necessary to localize causal variants in regulatory elements and identify the gene(s) regulated by that element.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the nature of GWAS loci.

claim: Multiple cell types contribute to emphysema.
source: Since multiple cell types contribute to emphysema, large-scale functional annotation projects such as the Genotype-Tissue Expression Project (GTEx) (GTEx Consortium, 2015) and the Encyclopedia of Regulatory Elements (ENCODE) (ENCODE Project Consortium, 2012) can be integrated with GWAS signals to identify candidate regulatory regions, tissues, and cell types of interest for more detailed functional characterization.
evidence: This is based on established biological knowledge.

claim: Large-scale functional annotation projects such as GTEx and ENCODE can be integrated with GWAS signals to identify candidate regulatory regions, tissues, and cell types of interest for functional characterization.
source: Since multiple cell types contribute to emphysema, large-scale functional annotation projects such as the Genotype-Tissue Expression Project (GTEx) (GTEx Consortium, 2015) and the Encyclopedia of Regulatory Elements (ENCODE) (ENCODE Project Consortium, 2012) can be integrated with GWAS signals to identify candidate regulatory regions, tissues, and cell types of interest for more detailed functional characterization.
evidence: This is a methodological approach based on inference and prior knowledge.

claim: Human emphysema is influenced by functional genetic variants that disrupt gene regulatory elements.
source: In this study, we hypothesized that human emphysema is influenced by functional genetic variants that disrupt gene regulatory elements.
evidence: This is the hypothesis of the study.

claim: The analysis identified rs1690789 as a high-probability functional variant in the GWAS-identified region near TGFB2.
source: This analysis identified rs1690789 as a high-probability functional variant in the GWAS-identified region near TGFB2.
evidence: This is supported by the integrative analysis performed.

claim: The region spanning rs1690789 interacts with the TGFB2 promoter region.
source: Using chromatin conformation capture, we confirmed that the region spanning this SNP interacts with the TGFB2 promoter region.
evidence: This is supported by chromatin conformation capture experiments.

claim: A ~100 bp segment containing rs1690789 increases TGFB2 expression in primary human lung fibroblasts.
source: Via CRISPR/Cas-9 targeted deletion, we then demonstrated that a ~ 100 bp segment containing rs1690789 increases TGFB2 expression in primary human lung fibroblasts, providing novel evidence that genetic variation affecting TGF-β signaling contributes to the genetic predisposition to emphysema.
evidence: This is supported by CRISPR/Cas-9 deletion experiments showing decreased expression upon deletion.

claim: Genetic variation affecting TGF-β signaling contributes to the genetic predisposition to emphysema.
source: Via CRISPR/Cas-9 targeted deletion, we then demonstrated that a ~ 100 bp segment containing rs1690789 increases TGFB2 expression in primary human lung fibroblasts, providing novel evidence that genetic variation affecting TGF-β signaling contributes to the genetic predisposition to emphysema.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: LHE measures were generated in 1519 subjects from the ECLIPSE Study.
source: To confirm these associations in an independent cohort and discover new genetic associations, we generated new LHE measures in 1519 subjects from the ECLIPSE Study, and we replicated the previously observed relationships between LHE pattern and GOLD (Global Initiative for Obstructive Lung Disease) spirometric grade (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the study design and data generation.

claim: The study replicated the previously observed relationships between LHE pattern and GOLD spirometric grade.
source: To confirm these associations in an independent cohort and discover new genetic associations, we generated new LHE measures in 1519 subjects from the ECLIPSE Study, and we replicated the previously observed relationships between LHE pattern and GOLD (Global Initiative for Obstructive Lung Disease) spirometric grade (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The combined GWAS meta-analysis identified 10 independent regions with genome-wide significant associations to at least one LHE phenotype.
source: In the combined GWAS meta-analysis, we identified 10 independent regions with genome-wide significant associations to at least one LHE phenotype, six of which had been previously described (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by the GWAS meta-analysis results shown in Table 1.

claim: Six of the 10 genome-wide significant regions had been previously described.
source: In the combined GWAS meta-analysis, we identified 10 independent regions with genome-wide significant associations to at least one LHE phenotype, six of which had been previously described (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with prior literature and shown in Table 1.

claim: One of the four novel associations is rs28929474, the pathogenic Glu→Lys substitution in SERPINA1 which is known to be associated with COPD.
source: One of the four novel associations is rs28929474, the pathogenic Glu→Lys substitution in SERPINA1 which is known to be associated with COPD.
evidence: This is supported by prior knowledge about SERPINA1 and COPD.

claim: There was no evidence of systematic inflation in the QQ-plots of the GWAS.
source: There was no evidence of systematic inflation in the QQ-plots of these GWAS (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by the QQ-plots shown in Figure 2.

claim: Four loci remained genome-wide significant after inverse normal transformation of LHE pattern phenotypes.
source: In this analysis, four loci remained genome-wide significant (loci on chromosome 15, 14, 11, and 1), two loci had p-values<5×10−7, and four associations to the panlobular and severe centrilobular patterns had notably lower p-values suggesting that these specific associations are driven by extreme phenotype values and should be interpreted with caution.
evidence: This is supported by sensitivity analysis data.

claim: Four associations to the panlobular and severe centrilobular patterns are driven by extreme phenotype values.
source: In this analysis, four loci remained genome-wide significant (loci on chromosome 15, 14, 11, and 1), two loci had p-values<5×10−7, and four associations to the panlobular and severe centrilobular patterns had notably lower p-values suggesting that these specific associations are driven by extreme phenotype values and should be interpreted with caution.
evidence: This is inferred from the sensitivity analysis results.

claim: Six individuals in ECLIPSE had imputed PiZZ genotypes for rs28929474.
source: However, when we examined the imputed genotypes of rs28929474, we identified six individuals in ECLIPSE with imputed PiZZ genotypes.
evidence: This is supported by examination of imputed genotype data.

claim: When subjects with imputed PiZZ genotypes were excluded, the association p-value for rs28929474 in ECLIPSE increased from 0.0004 to 0.003.
source: When we repeated the genetic analysis without these subjects, there was an increase in association p-value in ECLIPSE (0.003 versus 0.0004, consistent direction of effect), and the meta-analysis association p-value was 1.6 × 10−7.
evidence: This is supported by reanalysis of the genetic data.

claim: Five of the 10 LHE loci were associated to at least one of FEV1, FEV1/FVC, or COPD status at p<0.05 with a consistent direction of effect.
source: Five of the 10 LHE loci (lead variants rs56113850, rs796395, rs17368659, rs145770770, and the 15q25 locus) were associated to at least one of these outcomes at p<0.05 with a consistent direction of effect (Supplementary file 1 Table 4).
evidence: This is supported by lookup of variants in other GWAS studies.

claim: The only LHE associations that were nominally associated to smoking were the previously known smoking associations in the 15q25 and 19q13 loci.
source: To determine how many of our associations were also associated to smoking behavior, we queried our results against the UK Biobank Pheweb server GWAS for prior history of smoking, and we observed that the only associations that were nominally associated to smoking were the previously known smoking associations in the 15q25 and 19q13 loci (Supplementary file 1 Table 5).
evidence: This is supported by lookup of variants in smoking behavior GWAS.

claim: Four genome-wide significant LHE regions overlapped with eQTL regions with an estimated >80% probability of a shared causal variant.
source: Four genome-wide significant LHE regions overlapped with eQTL regions with an estimated >80% probability of a shared causal variant responsible for the GWAS and eQTL associations (Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by Bayesian colocalization analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: At GWAS p<5×10−5, 32 loci had a >80% estimated probability of having a shared causal GWAS-eQTL variant.
source: Of these loci, 32 had a > 80% estimated probability of having a shared causal GWAS-eQTL variant, and we identified the genes whose expression levels are altered by these loci (Supplementary file 1 Table 6).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis at a relaxed threshold.

claim: The most commonly enriched cell types in LHE GWAS regions were fibroblasts and fetal lung tissue.
source: The most commonly enriched cell types were fibroblasts and fetal lung tissue, as can be seen in the enrichment results for moderate centrilobular emphysema (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: There were 15, 25, and 1 cell types that exceeded the significance threshold for the moderate centrilobular, nonemphysematous, and severe centrilobular LHE phenotypes, respectively.
source: Out of 424 tested cell type annotations, there were 15, 25, and 1 cell type that exceeded the significance threshold for the moderate centrilobular, nonemphysematous, and severe centrilobular LHE phenotypes, respectively (Supplementary file 1 Table 7).
evidence: This is supported by enrichment analysis results.

claim: One of the top GWAS-eQTL colocalization signals associated with moderate centrilobular emphysema spans a 200 kb region that includes the 3' UTR of TGFB2 and extends 100 kb downstream.
source: One of the top GWAS-eQTL colocalization signals associated with the moderate centrilobular emphysema pattern spans a 200 kb region that includes the 3' UTR of TGFB2 and extends 100 kb downstream.
evidence: This is supported by the colocalization analysis.

claim: Multiple SNPs in the TGFB2 region were significantly associated with TGFB2 expression in human tissues from the GTEx project.
source: Multiple SNPs in this region were significantly associated with TGFB2 expression in human tissues from the GTEx project (Figure 5) with the highest colocalization present with the eQTL signal in cultured fibroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by eQTL data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The highest colocalization of GWAS and eQTL signals for TGFB2 was present in cultured fibroblasts.
source: Multiple SNPs in this region were significantly associated with TGFB2 expression in human tissues from the GTEx project (Figure 5) with the highest colocalization present with the eQTL signal in cultured fibroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: TGF-β signaling and fibroblasts have essential roles in lung repair pathways.
source: Given the essential roles of TGF-β signaling and fibroblasts in lung repair pathways, we selected this locus for further investigation.
evidence: This is based on established biological knowledge.

claim: rs1690789 is located at one of the GWAS association peaks and lies within a context-specific DNaseI peak.
source: rs1690789 is located at one of these GWAS association peaks and lies within a context-specific DNaseI peak (Panel C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5, Panel C.

claim: Sherlock analysis confirmed TGFB2 as a colocalization target for moderate centrilobular emphysema in fibroblasts.
source: Sherlock analysis for the moderate centrilobular GWAS results and GTEx eQTL data from fibroblasts, lung tissue, and whole blood confirmed TGFB2 as a colocalization target for moderate centrilobular emphysema in fibroblasts, and a total of nine colocalizing genes or transcripts were identified at a p-value<1×10−4 (Supplementary file 1 Table 8).
evidence: This is supported by Sherlock colocalization analysis.

claim: The GWAS signal in the TGFB2 region demonstrates two independent peaks of association spanning a recombination hotspot.
source: The GWAS signal in this region appears to demonstrate two independent peaks of association spanning a recombination hotspot, with the fibroblast eQTL signal appearing to colocalize with only one of these signals.
evidence: This is inferred from the GWAS data pattern.

claim: The fibroblast eQTL signal appears to colocalize with only one of the two independent GWAS peaks in the TGFB2 region.
source: The GWAS signal in this region appears to demonstrate two independent peaks of association spanning a recombination hotspot, with the fibroblast eQTL signal appearing to colocalize with only one of these signals.
evidence: This is inferred from the colocalization analysis.

claim: Conditional genetic association analysis confirmed the presence of two independent signals in the TGFB2 region.
source: We performed conditional genetic association analysis of this region, confirming the presence of two independent signals (secondary association lead SNP rs3009942 p=4.4×10−7, Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by conditional association analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: The secondary association lead SNP in the TGFB2 region is rs3009942 with p=4.4×10−7.
source: We performed conditional genetic association analysis of this region, confirming the presence of two independent signals (secondary association lead SNP rs3009942 p=4.4×10−7, Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by conditional association analysis.

claim: Adjusting for rs3009942 minimally attenuated the primary association at rs796395 (conditional p-value=3.3×10−7).
source: To confirm that these are independent signals, we also performed conditional association adjusting for rs3009942, which minimally attenuated the primary association (rs796395 conditional p-value=3.3×10−7).
evidence: This is supported by conditional association analysis.

claim: Seven variants in the TGFB2 region each have a >5% estimated likelihood to be causal.
source: Focusing on the primary association peak which colocalized with the fibroblast eQTL signal, we estimated the causal probability (i.e. the likelihood that each individual SNP is the causal variant) of each SNP in this region using the PICS method (Farh et al., 2015), identifying seven variants each with a > 5% estimated likelihood to be causal (Supplementary file 1 Table 9).
evidence: This is supported by PICS fine-mapping analysis.

claim: rs1690789 is the only variant in the set of seven high-probability causal variants predicted to have allele-specific effects on transcription factor occupancy.
source: We then queried whether any of these seven SNPs were predicted to alter transcription factor occupancy using the results of a previously published model developed from ENCODE data (Maurano et al., 2015), identifying rs1690789 (minor allele frequency of 0.48 in 1000 Genomes EUR population) as the only variant in this set predicted to have allele-specific effects on transcription factor occupancy.
evidence: This is supported by analysis using the CATO model.

claim: rs1690789 has a minor allele frequency of 0.48 in the 1000 Genomes EUR population.
source: We then queried whether any of these seven SNPs were predicted to alter transcription factor occupancy using the results of a previously published model developed from ENCODE data (Maurano et al., 2015), identifying rs1690789 (minor allele frequency of 0.48 in 1000 Genomes EUR population) as the only variant in this set predicted to have allele-specific effects on transcription factor occupancy.
evidence: This is data from the 1000 Genomes reference panel.

claim: rs1690789 lies within a DNaseI hypersensitivity peak identified in 13 cell types.
source: Using the ENCODE uniformly processed DNaseI hypersensitivity dataset of 125 cell types, we observed that rs1690789 lies within a DNaseI hypersensitivity peak identified in 13 cell types (Figure 5, Panel C).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of ENCODE DNaseI data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Eight of the 13 cell types with DNaseI peaks at rs1690789 were fibroblasts.
source: Eight of these 13 cell types were fibroblasts, although this peak was not universally detected in all fibroblast DNaseI experiments, suggesting that this may be a context-specific regulatory element or that DNaseI accessibility may be influenced by genetic variation in these cell types.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of ENCODE DNaseI data.

claim: The DNaseI peak at rs1690789 was not universally detected in all fibroblast DNaseI experiments.
source: Eight of these 13 cell types were fibroblasts, although this peak was not universally detected in all fibroblast DNaseI experiments, suggesting that this may be a context-specific regulatory element or that DNaseI accessibility may be influenced by genetic variation in these cell types.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of ENCODE DNaseI data.

claim: The rs1690789 region may be a context-specific regulatory element.
source: Eight of these 13 cell types were fibroblasts, although this peak was not universally detected in all fibroblast DNaseI experiments, suggesting that this may be a context-specific regulatory element or that DNaseI accessibility may be influenced by genetic variation in these cell types.
evidence: This is speculated based on the variable detection of DNaseI peaks.

claim: DNaseI accessibility at rs1690789 may be influenced by genetic variation in fibroblast cell types.
source: Eight of these 13 cell types were fibroblasts, although this peak was not universally detected in all fibroblast DNaseI experiments, suggesting that this may be a context-specific regulatory element or that DNaseI accessibility may be influenced by genetic variation in these cell types.
evidence: This is speculated based on the variable detection of DNaseI peaks.

claim: rs1690789 is located ~200 kb from the transcription start site of TGFB2.
source: Since rs1690789 is located ~200 kb from the transcription start site of TGFB2, we hypothesized that this region may regulate TGFB2 expression via a long-range chromatin interaction.
evidence: This is based on genomic position data.

claim: The rs1690789 region may regulate TGFB2 expression via a long-range chromatin interaction.
source: Since rs1690789 is located ~200 kb from the transcription start site of TGFB2, we hypothesized that this region may regulate TGFB2 expression via a long-range chromatin interaction.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the genomic distance.

claim: The 10 kb region containing rs1690789 contacts multiple upstream and downstream regions around TGFB2 in IMR90 human lung fibroblasts.
source: Using publicly available 4C-Seq chromatin conformation data from IMR90 human lung fibroblasts (Rao et al., 2014), we observed that the 10 kb region containing rs1690789 contacts multiple upstream and downstream regions around TGFB2 (Figure 7A), suggesting that this region is a hotspot of chromosomal interaction.
evidence: This is supported by 4C-Seq data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The rs1690789 region is a hotspot of chromosomal interaction.
source: Using publicly available 4C-Seq chromatin conformation data from IMR90 human lung fibroblasts (Rao et al., 2014), we observed that the 10 kb region containing rs1690789 contacts multiple upstream and downstream regions around TGFB2 (Figure 7A), suggesting that this region is a hotspot of chromosomal interaction.
evidence: This is inferred from the 4C-Seq data showing multiple contacts.

claim: 3C experiments detected interaction between the rs1690789-containing region and the TGFB2 promoter in lung fibroblasts.
source: Using the TGFB2 promoter region as the anchor region, we detected interaction between the rs1690789-containing region and the TGFB2 promoter in lung fibroblasts (Figure 7B), suggesting long range regulation of TGFB2 by the region containing rs1690789.
evidence: This is supported by 3C experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The rs1690789 region regulates TGFB2 via long-range regulation.
source: Using the TGFB2 promoter region as the anchor region, we detected interaction between the rs1690789-containing region and the TGFB2 promoter in lung fibroblasts (Figure 7B), suggesting long range regulation of TGFB2 by the region containing rs1690789.
evidence: This is inferred from the 3C data showing physical interaction.

claim: CRISPR/Cas-9 deletion of the ~100 bp region spanning rs1690789 resulted in reduced expression of TGFB2 in normal primary human lung fibroblasts.
source: With sufficient deletion efficiency of the region spanning rs1690789, we detected reduced expression of TGFB2 (Figure 8B and C, Supplementary file 1 Table 11), indicating that this distal genomic region has regulatory effects on the expression of TGFB2 in normal primary human lung fibroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by CRISPR/Cas-9 deletion experiments shown in Figure 8.

claim: The distal genomic region containing rs1690789 has regulatory effects on the expression of TGFB2 in normal primary human lung fibroblasts.
source: With sufficient deletion efficiency of the region spanning rs1690789, we detected reduced expression of TGFB2 (Figure 8B and C, Supplementary file 1 Table 11), indicating that this distal genomic region has regulatory effects on the expression of TGFB2 in normal primary human lung fibroblasts.
evidence: This is concluded from the CRISPR/Cas-9 deletion experiments.

claim: Previous GWAS studies have demonstrated that common genetic variation contributes to emphysema.
source: Previous GWAS studies have demonstrated that common genetic variation contributes to emphysema (Cho et al., 2015), likely through the perturbation of gene regulatory mechanisms (Castaldi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior GWAS studies.

claim: Common genetic variation likely contributes to emphysema through the perturbation of gene regulatory mechanisms.
source: Previous GWAS studies have demonstrated that common genetic variation contributes to emphysema (Cho et al., 2015), likely through the perturbation of gene regulatory mechanisms (Castaldi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The study identified 32 emphysema-associated loci at p<5×10−5 where it is likely that colocalized GWAS and eQTL signals arise from the same causal variant.
source: Using Bayesian colocalization, we identified 32 emphysema-associated loci at p<5×10−5 where it is likely that colocalized GWAS and eQTL signals arise from the same causal variant.
evidence: This is supported by Bayesian colocalization analysis.

claim: The 32 colocalized loci are putative and not confirmed disease variants due to the use of a relaxed GWAS significance threshold.
source: It should be noted that these are putative and not confirmed disease variants due to our use of a relaxed GWAS significance threshold and the inherent complexities of colocalization, which continues to be an area of active methodological development.
evidence: This is a caveat about the interpretation of the colocalization results.

claim: Multiple sources of publicly available and newly generated experimental data link rs1690789 to TGFB2 expression in fibroblasts.
source: For the genome-wide significant locus near TGFB2, multiple sources of publicly available and newly generated experimental data link a functional variant, rs1690789, to TGFB2 expression in fibroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by multiple lines of evidence presented in the study.

claim: Naturally occurring genetic variability in TGF-β signaling plays a causal role in the development of emphysema.
source: These data suggest that naturally occurring genetic variability in TGF-β signaling plays a causal role in the development of emphysema.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The TGF-β family of proteins constitutes a set of highly conserved signaling pathways that play a key role in human development and many other cellular functions.
source: The TGF-β family of proteins constitutes a set of highly conserved signaling pathways that play a key role in human development and many other cellular functions (Huminiecki et al., 2009; Massagué, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: TGF-β family proteins participate in normal lung development.
source: With respect to the lung, TGF-β family proteins participate in normal lung development and are dysregulated in COPD, emphysema, asthma, and pulmonary fibrosis (Verhamme et al., 2015; Morris et al., 2003; Thomas et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: TGF-β family proteins are dysregulated in COPD, emphysema, asthma, and pulmonary fibrosis.
source: With respect to the lung, TGF-β family proteins participate in normal lung development and are dysregulated in COPD, emphysema, asthma, and pulmonary fibrosis (Verhamme et al., 2015; Morris et al., 2003; Thomas et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Genetic variants near TGF-β superfamily members TGFB2, ACVR1B, LTBP4, and BMP6 have been identified in GWAS for lung function and COPD.
source: Genetic variants near TGF-β superfamily members TGFB2 (Castaldi et al., 2014; Cho et al., 2014), ACVR1B (Boueiz et al., 2019), LTBP4 (Wain et al., 2017), and BMP6 (Loth et al., 2014) have been identified in GWAS for lung function and COPD, but prior to this study the region near ACVR1B was the only one linked to a gene in the TGF-β pathway through functional studies (Boueiz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior GWAS studies.

claim: Prior to this study, the region near ACVR1B was the only TGF-β superfamily locus linked to a gene through functional studies.
source: Genetic variants near TGF-β superfamily members TGFB2 (Castaldi et al., 2014; Cho et al., 2014), ACVR1B (Boueiz et al., 2019), LTBP4 (Wain et al., 2017), and BMP6 (Loth et al., 2014) have been identified in GWAS for lung function and COPD, but prior to this study the region near ACVR1B was the only one linked to a gene in the TGF-β pathway through functional studies (Boueiz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to this study.

claim: The findings demonstrate that the emphysema-associated variant rs1690789 is located in an active gene regulatory region in human lung fibroblasts.
source: Our findings demonstrate that the emphysema-associated variant rs1690789 is located in an active gene regulatory region in human lung fibroblasts that interacts with the promoter region of TGFB2 and regulates TGFB2 expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: rs1690789 interacts with the promoter region of TGFB2.
source: Our findings demonstrate that the emphysema-associated variant rs1690789 is located in an active gene regulatory region in human lung fibroblasts that interacts with the promoter region of TGFB2 and regulates TGFB2 expression.
evidence: This is supported by chromatin conformation capture experiments.

claim: rs1690789 regulates TGFB2 expression.
source: Our findings demonstrate that the emphysema-associated variant rs1690789 is located in an active gene regulatory region in human lung fibroblasts that interacts with the promoter region of TGFB2 and regulates TGFB2 expression.
evidence: This is supported by CRISPR/Cas-9 deletion experiments.

claim: The analyses highlight the genetic and gene regulatory complexity of the TGFB2 region.
source: These analyses highlight the genetic and gene regulatory complexity of this region.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Conditional association analyses identified two independent associations with moderate centrilobular emphysema near TGFB2.
